recent_posts.title: AI and The Future of Gamedev
recent_posts.summary: A veteran game developer and senior aerospace software engineer argues that AI cannot fully automate game development because the field requires iterative testing, physical world modeling, and design thinking that mirrors unsolved real-world AI challenges. The author draws a parallel between AI's difficulty with physical tasks and its limitations in implementing complex game features like VR physics and multiplayer netcode. While acknowledging vibe coding has legitimate uses for simpler software, the author warns that replacing junior developers with AI agents risks cutting off the career ladder that produces senior engineers, and expresses concern about long-term code quality at companies relying heavily on AI-generated code.

recent_posts.title: Creating Proximity Chat in my Engineless VR Shooter
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares their journey building a proximity chat system from scratch for a VR shooter game made with Python and a custom engine. The implementation covers microphone input capture, spatial audio with OpenAL, audio streaming over networks with Opus compression, deferred rendering for lighting effects, SSAO implementation, and AABB physics for collision detection. The project includes building a tavern lobby map with custom decorations and integrating voice chat that adjusts volume based on player distance in 3D space.

recent_posts.title: Pygame Code Structure Guide
recent_posts.summary: A veteran Python game developer shares practical insights on code organization for Pygame projects, challenging traditional OOP principles like encapsulation and inheritance. The guide advocates for flat, globally accessible object structures over dependency injection, emphasizes pragmatism over perfect code, and provides concrete implementation patterns including element registries, file organization strategies, and import conventions. The author argues that game development's highly interconnected nature and frequent design changes require different structural approaches than typical software, prioritizing development speed and flexibility over rigid abstraction.

recent_posts.title: How to make VR games with Python #gamedev #python #vr
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares their experience building an online multiplayer VR shooter entirely in Python, detailing the technical architecture and libraries used. The implementation combines PyOpenXR for VR device interaction, ModernGL for 3D rendering, PyGLM for math operations, and custom networking code. The post explains how to handle eye tracking, render scenes to VR headsets, display desktop windows, manage UI elements with Pygame, load 3D models, handle audio with PyOpenAL, and implement multiplayer networking using a custom Python framework called Shobnet.

recent_posts.title: Recreating a Lost Minecraft Minigame in VR with Python
recent_posts.summary: A developer recreates the lost Minecraft minigame Turf Wars as a VR shooter using Python. The project combines building mechanics with gunplay, featuring a skill-based mining system where players use a chest-mounted pickaxe to break blocks by hitting weak points in sequence. The game mode involves two teams battling for territory, with kills expanding your buildable area. The developer discusses VR interface design challenges, implementing natural switching between building and shooting modes, and plans to add more classic Minecraft minigames to their multiplayer VR shooter called Gunslaw VR.

recent_posts.title: How to Make Multiplayer Python Games - Tutorial
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive tutorial covering Python network programming fundamentals for creating multiplayer games. Demonstrates building a client-server architecture using TCP sockets, threading for asynchronous communication, and binary data serialization. Shows implementation of an authoritative server that validates moves and broadcasts game state, with clients sending player actions. Covers practical considerations like error handling, connection management, and deployment to remote servers. Uses tic-tac-toe as the example game to illustrate core networking concepts applicable to various multiplayer game types.

recent_posts.title: Rendering 100,000 Steves with Python
recent_posts.summary: Rendering 100,000 objects in Python can be achieved by leveraging optimized dependencies and performing computation on the GPU. This approach minimizes the computational steps required in Python. By merging objects and embedding the origin data into vertices, shaders can handle object transformations, showing that Python can be more resourceful than often perceived.

recent_posts.title: How I made my Python VR shooter multiplayer
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the author's progress in making their Python VR shooter game, 'Gunslaw,' multiplayer. They detail the implementation of networking using shared objects, binary encodings for efficient data transmission, and item ownership systems to manage physics and interactions. The post also highlights plans for future game modes, the integration of the Steamworks SDK for avatars and usernames, and an invitation to join the game's Discord community. The aim is to make the game free-to-play and expand its player base through continuous updates and improvements.

recent_posts.title: Benefits of participating in game jams
recent_posts.summary: Participating in game jams can significantly enhance your skills as a game developer. These events require creating a game based on a theme within a limited time frame, pushing developers to commit to ideas, manage their time effectively, and complete projects. Game jams provide valuable experience in planning, organization, marketing, and offer extensive feedback from fellow developers, helping improve game design and launching successful games.
